blocks.text: Image of the week

blocks.alt: 1533 illustration of many fiery, serpent-like dragons streaking above a dark town
blocks.caption: Photograph: Christies

blocks.text: As anxieties around climate catastrophe and existential threats from new technology intensify, humanity turns to mass media to confirm its worst fears. That’s the idea behind this singular German “wonderbook” from the 1550s, which depicts sensationalised scenes of terror in watercolour and gouache. In it, a plague of locusts arrive in Poland on a “terrible wind” in 1527, the North Sea floods Frisia in 1230 and, in the image above, dragons fly over Bavaria in 1533. The Book of Miracles is expected to reach up to £1m at auction at Christies in London, where the public can see it in person before it is sold.

blocks.text: Masterpiece of the week
Portrait of a Woman by Workshop of the Master of the Holy Kindred , 1495-1500

blocks.alt: Portrait of a Woman by Workshop of the Master of the Holy Kindred, 1495-1500
blocks.caption: Photograph: The National Gallery, London

blocks.text: This face from the past is so alive, as if you met her in the flesh. That’s partly because the unknown artist has posed his unknown subject, who probably lived in Cologne, Germany, looking out of the painting to the side. She seems to be in conversation: there’s a sense of movement, energy, engagement. Then again this mobility must also belong to her, not just the artist’s bag of tricks. For she seems quite a character: her long, thin face, penetrating grey eyes, thin eyebrows and bow-shaped lips all suggest a strong personal presence. Fashionable, discreetly luxurious clothes and jewellery also make it clear she is a woman of substance. This panel was once joined by a hinge to another, with her facing the lost image on the other side of the diptych: but surely her worldly appearance doesn’t fit with it being a religious scene. Rather, she is looking confidently and with some sense of equality at her husband, presumably a wealthy burgher of Cologne. National Gallery, London
